html:
A naval expedition in 1025 in which the Chola emperor Rajendra I sent a fleet across the Bay of Bengal to attack Srivijaya, the trading empire that controlled the Strait of Malacca.

Rajendra's inscriptions list the places taken: Srivijaya's capital on Sumatra, Kadaram (Kedah) on the Malay peninsula, and a string of other ports. The Srivijayan king was captured and much treasure carried off. The motive was most likely trade. Srivijaya taxed the ships passing between India and China, and Tamil merchant guilds such as the Five Hundred of Ayyavole wanted freer passage.

It was a rare event: no other Indian state sent a war fleet so far. The Cholas did not try to hold the lands, but Srivijaya never fully recovered its grip on the straits, and Tamil traders grew stronger in the region. The raid came at the height of the dynasty begun by Rajendra's father Rajaraja I, in an age of Indian Ocean trade at full reach.
sum: A naval expedition in 1025 in which the Chola emperor Rajendra I sent a fleet across the Bay of Bengal to attack Srivijaya, the trading empire that controlled the Strait of Malacca.
